description: I am interested in space technology. I am making a presentation about the equipment NASA left behind on the moon & mars . I am working solo i am not looking for team members
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an educational storytelling project that explores the human-made equipment remaining on the Moon and Mars after NASA missions. It focuses on the Apollo Lunar Module descent stages, Lunar Roving Vehicles and scientific instruments on the Moon, as well as the landing equipment from the Perseverance mission on Mars, including its heat shield, parachute, backshell and descent stage. The project describes why certain mission components are not brought back to Earth and compares the equipment found on both planetary surfaces. To make the subject more engaging, it includes imaginative stories narrated from the perspectives of a lunar rover, a heat shield and a descent stage. These objects are valuable records of scientific progress, technological development and space exploration. The project also discusses the need to preserve these historical remains through location documentation, satellite-based observation and responsible protection of landing sites.
details: The main aim of this project is to introduce space heritage in a simple and engaging way through storytelling. The presentation is organised into seven slides and examines why spacecraft leave certain components behind after completing their missions. Factors such as restricted storage capacity, equipment weight, landing-specific components and scientific devices intended to remain on the surface are explained. The project describes the important objects found on the Moon, including Apollo Lunar Module descent stages, Lunar Roving Vehicles and scientific research instruments. It also examines the remains of the Mars 2020 Perseverance landing system, such as the heat shield, parachute, backshell and descent stage. The sequence of events involved in the rover's landing on Mars is also presented. A comparison between the Moon and Mars highlights the different types of exploration and equipment associated with each world. In addition, three fictional first-person narratives describe the experiences of a Lunar Rover, a heat shield and a descent stage. These narratives are creative interpretations and should not be considered actual recorded statements. The concluding section explains the historical and technological value of these objects and recommends methods for safeguarding space heritage, including documenting artifact positions, examining landing areas through satellite imagery and avoiding unnecessary contact with historic remains. PowerPoint slides with simple diagrams and shapes are used to communicate the information. AI assistance was used in developing the presentation content and design. The project aims to encourage students and the wider public to understand the achievements of space missions and recognise the importance of protecting their historical remains.
